units.explain: A generic descriptor that forwards attribute access on an owning object to that object's config dictionary. __init__ stores the config key name (also assigned to self.__name__) and an optional converter callable. __get__ on an instance (obj not None) reads obj.config[self.__name__]; if a converter was supplied it is applied to the raw value before returning. When accessed on the class (obj is None) the descriptor itself is returned, per the overloads. __set__ writes the value into obj.config under the stored name. Behavior depends on the owner exposing a .config attribute supporting item get/set; that owner boundary is not defined in this file.
units.summary: Descriptor forwarding attribute get/set to the owner's config dict, with optional value conversion.

extras.note: Class-level access (obj is None) returns the descriptor itself, not a config value.

relations.basis: Descriptor indexes obj.config, which is a Config instance in Flask apps (owner not shown in this file)

uncertainties: Behavior when the owner has no config attribute, or the config lacks the key (KeyError), is inferred from dict indexing, not proven here.

units.explain: A dict subclass that behaves like a plain dict but adds loaders for populating itself: from environment variables (from_envvar, from_prefixed_env), Python files (from_pyfile), objects or import strings (from_object), arbitrary file formats via a loader callable (from_file), and mappings (from_mapping). Only uppercase keys are inserted by the from_* loaders; from_prefixed_env instead inserts keys derived from env names after prefix stripping and __-splitting. __init__ seeds the dict with optional defaults and stores root_path, the base for resolving relative filenames in from_pyfile and from_file. Missing-file handling is governed by silent: with silent=True and a not-found errno (ENOENT/EISDIR, plus ENOTDIR in from_pyfile), the loader returns False; otherwise OSError is re-raised with strerror prefixed 'Unable to load configuration file (...)'. from_envvar raises RuntimeError when the env variable is unset and silent is False. from_prefixed_env always returns True after processing matching env vars in sorted order, swallowing any exception from the loads callable and keeping the raw string value. get_namespace extracts a prefixed subset of keys into a new dict with optional lowercasing and namespace trimming.
units.summary: Dict subclass that loads configuration from env vars, Python files, objects, loader-based files, and mappings.

relations.basis: ConfigAttribute indexes obj.config, which is a Config in Flask apps

uncertainties: The load callable in from_file is caller-supplied; graph shows multiple candidate targets (flask.json.load, JSONProvider.load), so the actual callee is caller-determined.
The loads callable in from_prefixed_env defaults to json.loads but the resolved callee among several json candidates is not determined from this file.
from_prefixed_env's broad except Exception swallows all loads errors, including non-parse errors; consequences for such errors are not further observable here.

units.explain: Initializes the config as a dict seeded with the given defaults (empty dict when defaults is None or falsy) and stores root_path as an attribute. root_path is later used by from_pyfile and from_file to resolve relative filenames. No validation of root_path or defaults is performed here.
units.summary: Seeds the dict with defaults and stores the root path for relative file resolution.

units.explain: Reads the named environment variable; if it is unset or empty, returns False when silent is True, otherwise raises RuntimeError stating the variable is not set. When set, delegates to from_pyfile(rv, silent=silent) and returns its boolean result, i.e. the pointed-to file is loaded relative to root_path with the same silent/OSError semantics as from_pyfile.
units.summary: Loads config from the file named by an environment variable, with optional silent failure.
uncertainties: Empty-string values are treated the same as unset (falsy check), inferred from the not rv branch.

units.explain: Iterates all environment variable names in sorted order and processes those starting with '{prefix}_' (prefix defaults to 'FLASK'). For each match, the prefix is stripped from the key and the string value is passed to the loads callable (default json.loads); any exception from loads is swallowed and the raw string is kept as the value. Keys containing '__' denote nesting: the key is split on '__', intermediate components are traversed (creating empty dicts for missing intermediate keys) and the tail component receives the value; keys without '__' are set directly. Always returns True. Note that keys set this way are not filtered for uppercase, and traversal assumes intermediate existing values are dicts; if an intermediate key exists with a non-dict value, indexing current[part] would fail, which is not handled here.
units.summary: Loads FLASK_-prefixed env vars in sorted order, JSON-parsing values and nesting keys split on double underscores.

relations.basis: graph evidence links the sorted iteration; not visible as a direct call in this source
default loads=json.loads; graph shows multiple candidate loads targets

uncertainties: Actual callee of loads and of sorted/os.environ iteration is not resolved from this source; graph lists several candidates.
Behavior when an intermediate '__' component exists as a non-dict value is not handled or specified in the code.

units.explain: Joins filename with root_path, then executes the file's bytecode in a fresh module namespace (types.ModuleType('config') with __file__ set), reading it in binary mode. On OSError: if silent is True and errno is ENOENT, EISDIR, or ENOTDIR, returns False; otherwise e.strerror is prefixed with 'Unable to load configuration file (...)' and the exception is re-raised. On success, passes the module to from_object, so only uppercase attributes become config keys, and returns True. Compilation or runtime errors inside the config file are not caught and propagate.
units.summary: Executes a Python config file and imports its uppercase attributes into the config.
uncertainties: Silent suppression applies only to the listed errno values; other OSErrors re-raise even with silent=True.
Exceptions raised while executing the file body (e.g. SyntaxError, NameError) propagate uncaught; their ordering relative to OSError handling follows the single except clause.

units.explain: Accepts either an import string or an object. If a string, the object is resolved via werkzeug.utils.import_string. Then for every attribute name in dir(obj) that is entirely uppercase (key.isupper()), the attribute's value is copied into the config via getattr. Lowercase and mixed-case attributes are skipped, and no exception handling wraps getattr, so property evaluation errors propagate. Returns None; existing keys are overwritten.
units.summary: Copies uppercase attributes from an object or imported module into the config.
uncertainties: import_string failure mode for invalid import names is not defined in this file.
getattr is invoked even on properties of classes, whose evaluation errors propagate unhandled.

units.explain: Joins filename with root_path, opens it in text mode ('r') or binary mode ('rb') depending on the text flag, and calls the caller-supplied load callable with the file handle to produce a mapping, which is then passed to from_mapping. On OSError: if silent is True and errno is ENOENT or EISDIR, returns False; otherwise e.strerror is prefixed with 'Unable to load configuration file (...)' and re-raised. Returns the boolean result of from_mapping, which is always True on success. Errors raised by the load callable itself are not caught.
units.summary: Loads a mapping via a caller-supplied loader from a text or binary file and merges uppercase keys.
uncertainties: The resolved load callable is caller-determined; the graph lists json.load and JSONProvider.load as candidates.
Silent suppression does not include ENOTDIR here, unlike from_pyfile.

units.explain: Merges an optional mapping and any keyword arguments into a fresh dict, then for each key that is entirely uppercase assigns the value into the config, overwriting existing keys. Lowercase keys are silently ignored. Always returns True; no exceptions are handled.
units.summary: Updates the config from a mapping and kwargs, keeping only uppercase keys; always returns True.
uncertainties: Mapping keys that are not strings would make key.isupper() raise AttributeError; this is not handled.

units.explain: Returns a new dict of config entries whose keys start with the given namespace prefix. For each matching key, the namespace prefix is stripped when trim_namespace is True, and the remainder is lowercased when lowercase is True; the value is copied unchanged. Non-matching keys are skipped. Iteration order follows the dict's own order; returns the collected dict.
units.summary: Collects config values whose keys share a prefix into a new dict with optional trimming and lowercasing.
uncertainties: The inventory id ends in 11515 while the source shows method get_namespace; assumed same symbol.

units.explain: Returns a string of the form '<ConfigName {dict contents}>' using the runtime type name and dict.__repr__ for the items, so subclasses report their own class name.
units.summary: Repr showing the runtime class name and the dict contents.
